newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria budgets $2.05 bln for 97 oil jv cash calls.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria budgets $2.05 bln for 97 oil jv cash calls.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has set aside $2.05 billion to pay for crude oil exploration and production joint ventures with foreign partners, the finance minister said on Monday.

"All cash calls up to December 31, 1996 have been paid, and the amount budgeted for 1997 is a similar amount to that which was spent last year," said Anthony Ani in his detailed breakdown of the annual budget.
Ani said 1997 crude oil production was estimated at around 2.04 million barrels per day.
The six major crude oil joint ventures are run by subsidiaries of Shell, Mobil, Chevron, Agip, Texaco and Elf.
State-run NNPC is the majority partner in all of them.

Military ruler General Sani Abacha on Saturday announced the annual budget, putting off further privatisation of state-run enterprises, including the oil industry, which had been widely called for by international donors and business.
